location: temporary: tests/fixtures/golden/clarity/ until the golden dataset's home is agreed
description: Ten synthetic high-clarity skills and ten unclear variants, one per skill, for the merged seven-criterion Clarity rubric (docs/evaluate-clarity.md). Not reviewed; for team analysis only.

criteria.purpose_and_trigger: The problem the skill solves, when to use it, and when not to are stated. (User criterion 4, problem part; previous rubric: trigger specificity.)
criteria.conciseness: Says what it needs to and stops. No padding, repetition, or long preambles. (User criterion 1.)
criteria.accessible_language: A reader with basic subject knowledge can follow it; jargon, acronyms and scientific names are avoided or explained at first use. (User criterion 2.)
criteria.readability: A person can tell what the skill accomplishes, and follow it, without an AI summarising or explaining it. (User criterion 3; previous rubric: human followability.)
criteria.structure_and_flow: Sections are organised, steps are in the order they must be done, and the writing flows. (User criterion 4, structure part; previous rubric: step ordering.)
criteria.verifiability: Required inputs, intermediate results and completion can be checked. (Previous rubric.)
criteria.failure_handling: Relevant failures and the recovery or stopping behaviour are clear. (Previous rubric.)

expected_properties: When to use and when not to use are both listed
evidence_quotes: The user asks to remove duplicates from a CSV file.
expectations.rationale: Trigger and limits (exact matches only, CSV only) are explicit.

expected_properties: Purpose stated in two sentences
Each section has one job and no restated content
evidence_quotes: Removes repeated rows from a CSV file so each record appears once.
expectations.rationale: The opening states the outcome and the safety guarantee in two sentences; everything else is steps or recovery.

expected_properties: Exact vs fuzzy matching is explained with an example rather than terminology
evidence_quotes: The user wants to merge rows that are only *similar* (such as "Jon Smith" and "John Smith"). This skill only removes exact matches.
expectations.rationale: Uses a concrete example instead of terms like 'fuzzy deduplication' or 'record linkage'.

expected_properties: Title, description and first line agree on what the skill does
evidence_quotes: description: Remove duplicate rows from a CSV file and report how many were removed.
expectations.rationale: A reader knows the outcome from the metadata alone.

expected_properties: Inputs confirmed, then options, then run, then report
evidence_quotes: Confirm the file path with the user and check that it exists.
expectations.rationale: Each step depends only on the ones before it.

expected_properties: Completion check stated
evidence_quotes: The rows-out count plus the removed count must equal the rows-in count.
expectations.rationale: A reader can check the result arithmetically.

expected_properties: Named failures with a recovery each
evidence_quotes: the column name is wrong. Show the user the header row and ask them to pick again.
expectations.rationale: Common failures stop or recover without guessing.

cases.limitations: Contains an inline script; judges may treat code length as verbosity. Annotators consider the script necessary content.

expected_properties: Concrete situations that trigger the skill
evidence_quotes: The user committed too early, to the wrong branch, or with a bad message, and wants to redo it.
expectations.rationale: Trigger is specific; pushed commits are excluded.

expected_properties: Four steps, one command each
No background history of Git
evidence_quotes: Undo it, keeping the changes staged:
expectations.rationale: Each step is one action with one command.

expected_properties: Why pushed commits are excluded is explained in everyday terms
evidence_quotes: Undoing it would rewrite history other people may have.
expectations.rationale: Explains the risk without assuming knowledge of rebasing or force-pushing.

expected_properties: Opening paragraph says what happens and that no work is lost
evidence_quotes: Takes back the last commit without losing any work.
expectations.rationale: Answers the reader's main worry (losing work) up front.

expected_properties: Safety check precedes the change
evidence_quotes: Show the user the commit that will be undone and get a yes:
expectations.rationale: Check, confirm, act, verify.

expected_properties: Observable result after the change
evidence_quotes: `git log -1 --oneline` should now show the commit *before* the one undone
expectations.rationale: The reader can confirm success with one command.

expected_properties: Edge case with stopping behaviour
Recovery path
evidence_quotes: the repository has only one commit. There is nothing earlier to go back to; tell the user and stop.
expectations.rationale: Covers the two realistic failures.

cases.limitations: Assumes the reader knows what a commit is; that is the stated basic subject knowledge.

expected_properties: Trigger phrased in the user's words
evidence_quotes: The user shares a transcript or notes and asks for a summary, decisions, follow-ups, or "what do I need to do".
expectations.rationale: Clear trigger; full-record requests excluded.

expected_properties: Each category is defined in one short phrase
evidence_quotes: List each **decision**: something the group agreed on.
expectations.rationale: Definitions are a clause long, not a paragraph.

expected_properties: No project-management jargon (RACI, deliverables, stakeholders)
evidence_quotes: List **open questions**: topics raised but not settled.
expectations.rationale: Every term is ordinary English.

expected_properties: The problem and the output are both stated in the opening
evidence_quotes: Long meeting notes hide the parts people actually need: what was decided and who is doing what.
expectations.rationale: One sentence tells the reader why the skill exists and what it produces.

expected_properties: Output template given after the steps that fill it
evidence_quotes: Return the result in this layout:
expectations.rationale: Read, extract three lists, format.

expected_properties: Every item traceable to the source
evidence_quotes: Every action item must trace back to something said in the transcript.
expectations.rationale: Checkable against the transcript.

expected_properties: Unlabelled speakers and truncated input handled
evidence_quotes: keep the action items but mark owners as "unclear" and tell the user.
expectations.rationale: Degrades openly instead of inventing.

cases.limitations: No tool use; tests clarity of a pure-writing skill.

expected_properties: Two triggers: identify and log

evidence_quotes: Use everyday bird names (such as "American robin"), not scientific names, unless the user asks for them.
**Size**, compared with a familiar bird (sparrow, robin, crow).
expectations.rationale: Directly targets the 'scientific species names' failure the criterion names.

expected_properties: Audience (casual birdwatcher) and the two jobs (identify, log) stated up front
evidence_quotes: Helps a casual birdwatcher put a name to a bird they saw and keeps a simple record of their sightings.
expectations.rationale: Reader knows who it is for and what it does from the first sentence.

expected_properties: Identify, confirm, then log
evidence_quotes: Ask the user which one matches.
expectations.rationale: Logging only happens after the user confirms.

expected_properties: Logged line read back

expected_properties: Vague input handled by asking
evidence_quotes: say so plainly and ask for a photo or one more detail, rather than guessing.
expectations.rationale: Stops guessing when evidence is thin.

expected_properties: The goal (smaller, still sharp) is stated in one line
evidence_quotes: This skill makes smaller copies that still look sharp on screen.

expected_properties: Prerequisite section before the steps

expected_properties: File counts compared

evidence_quotes: the folder has no `.jpg` or `.png` files.

expected_properties: Trigger and scope (two versions, counts only)

expected_properties: Two ready-made sentences for the two outcomes instead of a statistics lecture

expected_properties: Every technical term (A/B test, conversion, p-value) is defined in plain words at first use
evidence_quotes: An A/B test shows two versions of something (say, two sign-up pages) to different visitors and compares how often each one works.
visitors who did the thing being measured, such as signing up
The **p-value** is roughly the chance of seeing a difference this big if the two versions were actually the same.
expectations.rationale: Hardest jargon domain in the set; terms are unavoidable, so each is explained on first use.

expected_properties: States the user's real question

expectations.rationale: A non-statistician understands the skill's goal from this question alone.

expected_properties: Inputs listed in their own section before the steps

expected_properties: Input sanity check

cases.limitations: Contains a formula in code; a judge may count statistical code as jargon. Annotators treat code blocks as instructions for the agent, not reader-facing prose.
